findings.claim: t1 renders DashboardHeader only with serviceCount={6}, which equals the fixture's service count, so a masthead that hard-codes the literal text '6 services monitored' instead of reading the prop passes. Reproduced in a scratch copy: replacing the prop expression with the literal 6 in an otherwise solved starter still gives 8/8 passed. The test title ('computed service count') and the claimed objective components-and-jsx#o3 (embed an expression in curly braces to display a computed value) are therefore not actually verified. Rated medium rather than high because passing requires deliberately typing a literal against the explicit TASK 1 instruction; JSX conversion itself is verified.
findings.recommendation: Render the header with at least two different counts (for example rerender with serviceCount={4}, or render 6 then 11) and assert the banner text follows the prop each time.

findings.claim:
The 'Down now' check only asserts the list equals ['Email Relay'] after hiding Catalog API, which never changes the down set. A hard-coded
  • Email Relay
    • (or a list derived from the imported initialServices instead of the services state) passes. Reproduced in a scratch copy: a correct solution modified to (a) hard-code a single
  • Email Relay
    • , or (b) filter/map the imported initialServices instead of the services state, still gives 8/8 passed in both cases. The task-8 requirement 'derive it from the services state with filter and map' and the comment 'The Down now panel is derived from the services state' are unverified, and both wrong versions keep showing Email Relay in the app after it is hidden, i.e. the test accepts a wrong solution.
findings.recommendation: After the existing assertions, hide Email Relay and assert the Down now list becomes empty (no listitems), which a hard-coded or initialServices-derived list cannot satisfy.

findings.claim: On the shipped starter, t4, t5, t7 and t8 fail only because Panel (task 2) drops its children, so App renders no cards; all four report 'Unable to find an accessible element with the role "heading" and name "Checkout API"' (or no heading) rather than a task-specific message. Verified: with only Panel fixed, they then fail for their own reasons (stray 0, filter, acknowledge, hide). lab.json failingTests is still satisfied, but a learner who jumps to task 5 or 7 sees an error unrelated to that task, and the README does not mention the coupling (the part-2 README does document its t1 coupling).
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line README note under 'How to test' that tasks 4, 5, 7 and 8 render the whole App and only show their own failure once task 2 (Panel children) is done.

findings.claim: README task 8 says to 'key the cards by the service itself rather than the array index'. Read literally, key={service} passes an object as the key; React stringifies it to '[object Object]' for every card, giving duplicate keys. Verified in a scratch copy that t8 does reject key={service} (fails at 'Runbook: runbook/checkout-api'), so this is a wording problem that sends a learner who follows the README literally into a confusing failure, not a test gap. The TASK 8 (part 2) comment in App.jsx is more precise ('something that identifies the service itself').
findings.recommendation: Reword to 'key the cards by a stable value from the service, such as its id, rather than the array index'.

findings.claim: Several claimed objectives are only partly scored and cleanup.notes carries no partial-objective note (the part-2 lab.json does): usestate#o3 - a single non-updater setter call that adds three passes t6 without any updater function; conditional-display#o3 - guarding the MaintenanceNotice element at the call site passes t4 without the component returning null; project-structure#o2 - t3 imports StatusBadge.jsx directly, so ServiceCard.jsx can keep its own local StatusBadge/STATUS_LABELS copy and never import the module. Each was reproduced in a scratch copy by modifying a correct solution: all three variants still give 8/8 passed. These are behaviour-equivalent alternatives, so the tests are not wrong, but the objective claims overstate what is verified.
findings.recommendation: Add a partial-objective sentence to cleanup.notes naming these clauses, or (for project-structure#o2) add a behavioural check such as vi.mock of StatusBadge.jsx and asserting ServiceCard renders the mocked badge.

findings.claim: The config comment says fileParallelism:false makes Vitest 'Run files one at a time in name order so the summary is deterministic and matches expected/on-completion.txt'. Observed with Vitest 4.1.12: starter run order was t8, t7, t5, t4, t2, t1, t6, t3 and the solved run t4, t5, t8, t6, t7, t2, t1, t3; Vitest's sequencer does not sort by name. expected/on-completion.txt and lab.json correctly say lines may print in any order, so only the comment is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Change the comment to say files run one at a time (no parallel file workers) and that file order may vary, matching expected/on-completion.txt.

findings.claim: The TASK 1 masthead uses , but the starter ships no public/beacon.svg (no public/ directory at all), so in the optional 'npm run dev' view the converted masthead shows a broken image. Tests are unaffected (jsdom does not load images).
findings.recommendation: Ship a small license-clean starter/public/beacon.svg, or point the example at an asset that exists.

findings.claim: Setup says 'From this lab folder: cd tests, npm ci', then the optional block runs 'cd starter' with no reset. A learner following the blocks in sequence is inside tests/ and 'cd starter' fails (no such directory).
findings.recommendation: Use 'cd ../starter' in the optional block, or restate 'From the lab folder' before it.
